newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels kill two, bomb hurts three in Algeria - paper.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill two, bomb hurts three in Algeria - paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem guerrillas machinegunned a passenger van in Algeria, killing two people and wounding seven, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.
The van was carrying nine people from Tafrana village to a weekly market in the neighbouring town of Bathia in Ain Defla province, 130 km (80 miles) southwest of Algiers, said Al Khabar newspaper.
The two who died in Monday's attack were an elderly man and one in his 20s, it added.

The same day, a bomb exploded on a railway near Enahs village in Blida region, about 50 km (30 miles) south of the Algerian capital. Three men carrying out maintenance work were wounded, Al Khabar said.
The latest attacks on civilians are likely to fan opposition politicians' assaults in the multiparty National Assembly (lower house) on the government over security policy.
In the past two months, more than 700 people, including children and pregnant women, have been killed, bringing angry charges over lack of government action.
Opposition deputies in the house during more than 50 hours of debates broadcast live on Algerian state-run television have been grilling Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia over the continuing killings.
They also cast doubt on his ambitious programme to create 1.2 million jobs and build 800,000 housing units in the next three years, unless the authorities restore peace.
Ouyahia, whose supporters said opposition deputies were using the debate to improve their chances in local elections to be held in October, is expected to reply to his critics on Tuesday.
About 1,000 people -- including 300 rebels -- have been reported killed since last June 5 when the Algerians voted in an election for the 380-member house.
Algeria's leaders hoped that the vote, which resulted in 10 political parties and 11 independents entering parliament, would help bring a return to calm.
About 60,000 people have died in violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
